skill.name: create-plan
skill.description: Create concise coding plans that define scope, ordered action items, validation steps, risks, and open questions.
skill.summary: Create structured implementation plans for coding tasks.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks in SKILL.md, not executable code. The skill is prompt-only, read-only, and focused on generating implementation plans. No semantic evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or abusive behavior was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses Markdown inline backticks around file and directory names such as README.md and docs/. It does not instruct execution of shell commands or Ruby backticks.
Line 42 begins a fenced Markdown template for the assistant output format. The block contains plan headings and placeholders, not executable shell content.

content.value_statement: Planning coding work can be hard when requirements, files, tests, and risks are unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce concise implementation plans.
actual_capabilities: Scans repository documentation and likely relevant files before planning.
Defines what is in scope and what is out of scope.
Creates ordered action items from discovery through validation and rollout.
Includes tests, edge cases, and risks when they apply.
Limits follow-up questions to blocking unknowns.
Formats the final answer as a concise plan.
limitations: It produces plans only and does not write or update files.
It is designed for coding tasks, not general project management.
It depends on the available repository context and user prompt.
It may need clarification when requirements are incomplete.

use_cases.title: Plan a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Turn a reported defect into scoped investigation, fix, test, and rollout steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature Change
use_cases.description: Convert a feature request into ordered implementation work with validation and risk checks.

use_cases.title: Review Work Before Assignment
use_cases.description: Create a concise task plan that helps estimate effort and identify blocking questions.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Task Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a simple plan for a clear coding task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise plan for this coding task: [describe the task]. Include scope, ordered action items, validation, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Repository-Aware Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants a plan based on the current project structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository context and create a plan for [task]. Mention likely files, tests to run, risks, and any blocking questions.

prompt_templates.title: Feature Implementation Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: A product engineer needs a structured plan for a user-facing change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for [feature]. Separate in-scope and out-of-scope work, then order the steps from discovery through rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Risk-Aware Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: A lead needs a plan for a complex change with dependencies.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a risk-aware plan for [complex change]. Include affected modules, migration or rollout concerns, validation strategy, edge cases, and up to three open questions.

output_examples.input: Create a plan to add password reset to the application.
output_examples.output: A concise plan with scope boundaries, account flow review, email token design, tests for expiration and reuse, and rollout checks.

output_examples.input: Plan a fix for intermittent checkout failures.
output_examples.output: A focused debugging plan covering logs, payment boundaries, retry behavior, regression tests, and release risk.

output_examples.input: Create a plan before refactoring the settings page.
output_examples.output: A scoped refactor plan with likely files, component split steps, visual validation, accessibility checks, and open questions.

best_practices: Provide the specific coding goal and any known constraints.
Let the assistant inspect relevant docs and files before planning.
Ask for validation and risk items when the change affects users.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for broad strategy work unrelated to code.
Requesting implementation details before the scope is clear.
Skipping validation steps for risky or user-facing changes.

faq.question: Does this skill edit files?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to operate in read-only mode and produce a final plan.

faq.question: What kinds of tasks work best?
faq.answer: It works best for coding tasks such as bug fixes, feature changes, refactors, and validation planning.

faq.question: Can it ask follow-up questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks at most one or two questions when the missing information blocks a responsible plan.

faq.question: What format does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces a short plan with scope, ordered action items, and open questions when needed.

faq.question: Does it include tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow asks for at least one validation or test item when applicable.

faq.question: Can teams use it for review?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create concise plans that support task review, estimation, and handoff.
